header.opfunu_install: uv venv + uv pip install opfunu numpy setuptools<81 (PyPI, scratchpad-only)
header.tolerance_rationale: 1e-8 relative: independent summation order across sezgi (Rust), the compiled C reference, and opfunu (numpy) means bit-exactness is not expected. In practice sezgi vs the compiled C measured far tighter -- max relative delta 5.7e-15 over all 132 probe points in this task's own cross-check (near f64 machine epsilon), consistent with T5-T7's own reviews (~1e-10).

probe_points.o: the official CEC 2022 shift vector (component 1's row for hybrid/composition fids), first `dim` values of shift_data_<fid>.txt's first line -- read directly from crates/problems/data/cec2022/ (byte-identical to the C reference's own input_data/, verified via diff this task).
probe_points.random: numpy.random.default_rng(seed=20220601 + fid*100 + dim).uniform(-80.0, 80.0, dim) -- one independent seeded draw per (fid,dim) combination, fully reproducible.

header.dims: {2,10,20} for fid in 1..=5,9..=12; {10,20} for fid in 6..=8 (fid 6-8 reject dim=2, no shuffle_data_{6,7,8}_D2.txt vendored upstream, mod.rs module doc's T6 addendum).

divergence_classes.adjudicated-f3: PRE-ADJUDICATED (milestone controller ruling, mod.rs module doc 'F3' discrepancy note). opfunu follows the printed report's Expanded Schaffer's formula (scale 0.5/100, full rotation, escaffer6-style). The compiled C reference's fid-3 dispatch (`case 3: schaffer_F7_func(...)`) calls a DIFFERENT function (the f16 Schaffer's-F7 core) with sh_rate=1.0 (no scale) and, due to a buffer-reuse bug in schaffer_F7_func, no effective rotation either -- only the shift `x-o3` reaches the formula. sezgi replicates the C (code-over-report ruling); opfunu does not.
divergence_classes.adjudicated-f4: PRE-ADJUDICATED (mod.rs 'F4' discrepancy note). opfunu's non_continuous_rastrigin_func applies the report's step-quantization transform. The compiled C's step_rastrigin_func computes the quantized value into buffer `y` but then calls sr_func on the UNMODIFIED `x`, never reading `y` again -- the quantization is dead code, so the C's actual output is PLAIN Rastrigin. sezgi replicates the C; opfunu follows the report's (unreachable-in-the-C) intent.
divergence_classes.adjudicated-f5: PRE-ADJUDICATED (mod.rs 'F5' discrepancy note). opfunu applies the report's printed Eq (20) scale 5.12/100 (identical to Eq (19)'s Rastrigin scale directly above it -- almost certainly a PDF copy-paste typo). The compiled C's levy_func calls sr_func(...,1.0,...) -- sh_rate=1.0, no scale. sezgi replicates the C; opfunu follows the report's printed (probably erroneous) scale.
divergence_classes.adjudicated-f7-hybrid: PRE-ADJUDICATED (mod.rs fid-7 'VERIFIED DISCREPANCY (severe)' note). opfunu's F72022 evaluates the SchafferF7 component on its correctly-assigned last shuffled segment (idx6 = f_shuffle[n5:ndim]). The compiled C's schaffer_F7_func, called as hf10's 6th component, reads the GLOBAL `y[0..]` buffer from index 0 regardless of the pointer offset it was called with -- so it always reads a PREFIX of the whole shuffled vector (landing in the HGBat/Katsuura segments), and the true last segment is never read (verified: perturbing it changes the C's output by exactly 0.0). sezgi replicates this bug exactly (SchafferF7Buggy); opfunu implements the 'intended' (bug-free) behavior.
divergence_classes.opfunu-f1-zakharov-weight: NEW (found this task, opfunu 1.0.4 bug, not a report/code divergence). opfunu.utils.operator.zakharov_func computes `temp = np.sum(0.5 * x)` -- NO per-index weight. The compiled C's zakharov_func computes `sum2 += 0.5*(i+1)*xi` (1-based index weight) -- this IS present in the executed C and in sezgi's f1_base (`0.5 * (i + 1) as f64 * zi`), matching the classic (CEC-standard) Zakharov formula; the module doc's transcribed report excerpt just lost the subscript in pdftotext extraction, which is a transcription artifact, not a functional discrepancy -- sezgi's actual code already carried the index weight correctly. Verified: at a probed point, the weighted formula reproduces the compiled C's value (1089880523.9514904) exactly; the unweighted formula reproduces opfunu's diverging value (12129492.01288766).
divergence_classes.opfunu-hybrid-shuffle-rotate-order: NEW (found this task, opfunu 1.0.4 bug). For fid 6/7/8, opfunu shuffles the SHIFT-ONLY vector and THEN rotates it: `z = x - f_shift; z1 = concatenate(z[idx1], z[idx2], ...); mz = dot(f_matrix, z1)`. The compiled C (hf02/hf06/hf10) rotates the WHOLE vector ONCE via sr_func (full shift+rotate) and only THEN shuffles the ROTATED result: `sr_func(x,z,nx,Os,Mr,1.0,s_flag,r_flag); y[i]=z[S[i]-1];` (mod.rs module doc, T6's 'Shuffle' section, quoted). Permutation and matrix multiplication do not commute for a generic (non-permutation-invariant) rotation matrix M, so opfunu's mz = M*(P*z) differs from the C's y = P*(M*z) on essentially every point where the shift is nonzero. Verified: sezgi's fid-6 dim-10 value at a probed random point (16910793470.687101) matches the compiled C to 1e-15 relative; opfunu's value (22531324832.483086) diverges by ~33%. fid 8's much larger relative deltas (up to ~1e12) are attributed to this same root cause amplified by the chaotic sensitivity of grie_rosen_cec_func's cos(temp) term and katsuura_func's dimension-scaled exponential product to the resulting different input vector, not a further independent bug (not exhaustively re-derived given diminishing returns; the root-cause class is verified via source comparison and the fid-6 case above).
divergence_classes.opfunu-composition-shift-o1: NEW (found this task, opfunu 1.0.4 bug; PRIMARY root cause for fid 9-12's divergence). Every composition function (F92022 through F122022) computes EVERY component's rotated/scaled input `z_i` using `x - self.f_shift[0]` -- component 0's (o_1's) shift row -- for ALL i, e.g. F122022: `z1 = dot(f_matrix[ndim:2*ndim,:], 5.12*(x - self.f_shift[0])/100)` (component 1's z, but still `f_shift[0]`). The compiled C's cf01/cf02/cf06/cf07 pass each component its OWN shift row: `rastrigin_func(x,&fit[1],nx,&Os[1*nx],&Mr[1*nx*nx],1,r_flag)` (component i's g_i call uses `&Os[i*nx]`, verified by direct reading for every cf01/02/06/07 component). Only opfunu's WEIGHT function `w_i = calculate_weight(x - self.f_shift[i], ...)` correctly uses each component's own shift -- the mismatch is confined to the g_i INPUT. This single bug is the primary driver of fid 9-12's broad disagreement on non-o points (verified structurally against the quoted C source; sezgi's comp_shift_scale_rotate correctly uses `self.comp_shift[idx]`, each component's own row).
divergence_classes.opfunu-f9-r-flag: NEW, SECONDARY (compounds opfunu-composition-shift-o1 for fid 9). The compiled C's cf01 hardcodes r_flag=0 for its 5th component (the 2nd Ellipsoidal call): `ellips_func(x,&fit[4],nx,&Os[4*nx],&Mr[4*nx*nx],1,0);` -- literal `0`, ignoring the outer r_flag parameter (every other cf01 component passes the outer r_flag, which is always 1 from cec22_test_func's dispatch). sezgi's composition_spec(9) encodes this exactly (5th tuple entry `(Ellipsoidal, false, ...)`, verified by its own `composition_spec_matches_the_c_sources_constant_tables` unit test). opfunu's F92022 always rotates every component (`z4 = dot(f_matrix[4*ndim:5*ndim,:], x - f_shift[0])`, no r_flag=0 special case), so it also disagrees with the C on this component even independent of the shift-row bug above.
divergence_classes.opfunu-f10-r-flag: NEW, SECONDARY (compounds opfunu-composition-shift-o1 for fid 10). The compiled C's cf02 hardcodes r_flag=0 for its Schwefel component: `schwefel_func(x,&fit[0],nx,&Os[0*nx],&Mr[0*nx*nx],1,0);` -- literal `0`. sezgi's composition_spec(10) encodes this (`(Schwefel, false, 1.0)` as the first tuple entry). opfunu's F102022 always rotates every component (`z0 = dot(f_matrix[:ndim,:], (1000./100)*(x - f_shift[0]))`, no r_flag=0 special case).
divergence_classes.opfunu-f11-rosenbrock-shift: NEW, SECONDARY (compounds opfunu-composition-shift-o1 for fid 11). The compiled C's rosenbrock_func internally applies `z[0]+=1.0; z[i+1]+=1.0;` ('shift to origin', module doc's F2 note) AFTER its own sr_func call -- this applies inside every Rosenbrock use, including fid 11's 4th composition component. opfunu's F92022 correctly adds this inline (`z0 = dot(...) + 1`) for ITS Rosenbrock component, but F112022's Rosenbrock component omits it entirely (`z3 = dot(f_matrix[3*ndim:4*ndim,:], 2.048*(x-f_shift[0])/100); g3 = lamdas[3] * self.g3(z3)` where `self.g3 = operator.rosenbrock_func`, called with its default `shift=0.0`).
